concerns.text: The plan only performs a *post‑hoc* simulation‑based power analysis after the data are collected. There is no a priori power target or sample‑size justification, so the study may proceed with insufficient species (e.g., <15) and lack the ability to detect a moderate effect, violating the requirement for adequate statistical power.

Using species‑mean early‑life telomere length and maximum lifespan conflates within‑species variation and may not reflect the biological construct of interest. This aggregation threatens construct validity because the predictor and outcome are measured at different biological levels (individual vs. species) and may be biased by outlier individuals or captive lifespan records.

Confound control is limited to body mass and migration status. Important ecological covariates (e.g., diet, habitat, metabolic rate) and measurement‑method effects (TRF vs. qPCR) are not modeled, and the interaction model is automatically skipped when N < 30, potentially biasing conclusions in low‑power scenarios.
